meta.note: Every entry was requested and its wording read in this session on 2026-11-20. Where a page could not be reached from this environment, that is stated rather than worked around. Quotes are copied, not paraphrased; ellipses mark text left out.

sources.title: Amazon Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.page_date: not shown in the section read; Amazon displays the current version
sources.used_for: Section 5, Identifying Yourself as an Associate — the required disclosure wording, and the reason it appears on every page.
sources.quote: You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: “As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.”

sources.title: Amazon Associates Program Policies
sources.used_for: Participation Requirements 2(a) and 2(b): Special Links must use the assigned Associates ID; the tag must appear as a parameter in each link URL; and price/availability may only be shown where Amazon serves the data or it arrives via Creators API / PA API.
sources.quote: Special Links must use the Associates ID we have assigned to you. … you must include your Associates ID or “tag” (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site. … your Site may only show prices and availability if: (a) we serve the link in which that price and availability data are displayed, or (b) you obtain Product pricing and availability data via Creators API or PA API…
sources.finding: This is the clause that made the untagged destination links a defect rather than a preference: the tag is required in the URL of each link, not merely somewhere in the session.

sources.title: 16 CFR Part 255 — Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising, § 255.0(f)
sources.publisher: U.S. Federal Trade Commission, published in the eCFR (U.S. Government Publishing Office)
sources.used_for: The regulatory definition of “clear and conspicuous”, including the requirement that an internet disclosure be unavoidable — the reason the strip sits above the masthead.
sources.quote: “clear and conspicuous” means that a disclosure is difficult to miss (i.e., easily noticeable) and easily understandable by ordinary consumers. … In any communication using an interactive electronic medium, such as social media or the internet, the disclosure should be unavoidable. The disclosure should not be contradicted or mitigated by, or inconsistent with, anything else in the communication.

sources.title: FTC Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking (business guidance FAQ)
sources.page_date: no date shown on the page as served
sources.used_for: Practical placement guidance: a disclosure at the bottom of a page may be missed, and a disclosure is more likely to be seen close to the recommendation. Cited as guidance; the binding definition above is quoted from the regulation instead.
sources.status: linked, not quoted — the sentence this site relies on was verified against the FTC's own PDF, and the regulation is quoted directly at SRC-03

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google
sources.used_for: Confirms that rel="sponsored" is Google's documented marker for paid or advertising links, and that multiple rel values may be combined.
sources.quote: Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value.

sources.title: Understanding ASINs: your guide to Amazon’s product identification system
sources.publisher: Amazon — Sell on Amazon (official seller site)
sources.used_for: The definition of an ASIN and its length, used to show that a nine-character short-link code is not an ASIN. Replaces FLG-011, which recorded that this definition could not be reached.
sources.quote: “ASIN” stands for “Amazon Standard Identification Number.” It’s a unique 10-character alphanumeric code assigned to every product listed in the Amazon store. … The ASIN appears after “/dp/”.

sources.title: What is the application review process?
sources.page_date: no date shown on the page as served
sources.used_for: The account gate: at least three qualifying sales within the first 180 days, original content at roughly ten posts, rejection if the site does not meet the bar, and — the relevant part here — that Amazon lists untagged product links as a reason applications are rejected.
sources.quote: After you sign up, our Associates team will check your application once you’ve driven qualified sales (we require at least three within the first 180 days). … All Sites must have robust original content (even when advertising is removed) – a good rule of thumb is at least 10 posts. … we will reject applications if they do not meet these standards. … Associates special links are the identifiers (e.g. abcd-20) embedded in Amazon product links. These tags must be embedded in your Amazon product links on the site(s) declared in your application.
sources.finding: This is the single most consequential source for the plan: it ties the tag defect to account rejection, and it sets a ten-post content bar the site currently clears on count but not on originality.

sources.title: Cook to a Safe Minimum Internal Temperature
sources.used_for: The only food-safety temperature figures quoted anywhere on this site. Cited instead of the FSIS air-fryer page, which could not be reached from the build environment.
sources.quote: Always use a food thermometer to check whether meat has reached a safe minimum internal temperature that is hot enough to kill harmful germs that cause food poisoning.
